text: This chapter is one continuous capstone project, built across four lessons: define it here, build the orchestration layer next, add error handling and cost tracking after that, then review the finished architecture. This lesson is the scoping work every real hybrid project needs before any code gets written.

The capstone: estimate the ground-state energy of a small molecular system, as one input feature to a larger portfolio-risk model, run as a daily batch job. Applying the four-question method from Chapter 1's lab: a classical optimizer drives an ansatz circuit — Pattern A. The QPU evaluates a Hamiltonian expectation value. A six-parameter ansatz over eighty iterations comes out to one thousand forty circuit evaluations. And yes, that scale exists on today's hardware.
Here's the real device this whole project targets — Rigetti Ankaa-3, exactly as it appears on Amazon Braket, with real per-task and per-shot pricing attached.

And here's the budget, sized before any code gets written. Thirteen evaluations per iteration, batched into one submission, costs twelve dollars. Eighty iterations: nine hundred sixty dollars for one run. But if the real plan is running this daily, that's twenty-one thousand one hundred twenty dollars a month — a number that changes a go or no-go decision, flagged now, not after Lesson 21's cost tracking is built.

This project was scoped against a real catalog of quantum algorithms, the same four-question method from the architecture lab — and the success criteria here are entirely about classical engineering quality, not about beating a classical baseline, because that's not what this capstone is testing.

Next lesson takes this approved brief and builds the actual orchestration layer — the state machine, the batched submission strategy, and the job-lifecycle handling that will run this eighty-iteration loop for real.
